These applications for anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973,
are filed by accused Nos.1 and 2 in Crime No.28 of 2024 of Perumbavoor Police Station, Ernakulam,
registered under Sections 354, 376(2)(n), 376(3), 366-A of IPC and Sections 3(a), 4, 5l, 5m, 6, 7, 8,
9(i), 9(m), 10 and 21 of POCSO Act.

2. The prosecution allegation is that, the 1st accused, who is an octogenarian, committed rape on the victim girl, who was aged only 10, and even after the victim intimating that fact to the 2nd accused,
who is her mother, she concealed it without informing the same to the authorities concerned.
Moreover, the 2nd accused offered the victim to the 1st accused for committing sexual assault on her.

3. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the Sainaba Mymoon vs State Of Kerala on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94101617/
2 defacto complainant/additional 2nd respondent.
4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail applications B.A. Nos.397 and 571 of 2024 5.

The additional 2nd respondent, who is the victim filed affidavits in both the petitions, stating that the complaint was made on a mistake of fact based on some false information provided by a family friend.

Now, she has realised that mistake and she has no objection in allowing the bail applications of accused Nos.1 and 2.
6.
On instructions, learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the victim girl was asserting the allegations against the accused in her 164 statement also, and the offences alleged are of serious nature.
So the petitioners are not entitled for pre-arrest bail.
7. The alleged incident occurred while the victim was 10 years old.
She lodged the complaint after eight years.

Considering the delay in making the complaint and also considering the affidavits now filed by the victim girl, this Court is inclined to allow these applications on the following terms:-
(i) The petitioners shall surrender before the Investigating Officer on or before 23.02.2024 and subject themselves for interrogation.

(ii) In the event of arrest the petitioners shall be B.A. Nos.397 and 571 of 2024 released on bail on executing bond for Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees fifty thousand only) by each of them, with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the arresting officer.
(iii) Thereafter, the petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when directed.
(iv) Petitioners shall not influence or intimidate the witnesses or tamper with the investigation.
(v) Petitioners shall not commit any offence, while on bail.
In case of violation of the bail conditions, the trial court is empowered to cancel the bail, in accordance with law.
